chapter: Hampton, Blue Note and the electric guitar
title: Playing his first electric guitar, a Gretsch
summary: He bought a cheap Gretsch electric and describes playing lighter, sustained notes and no feedback problems.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But that was the first time, I think, you used an electric guitar.
On a recording. What kind of equipment were you using, do you remember?
I didn't realize that they made Gretsch -- 1940?
Yeah, but I got it cheaper. That's why I bought it.
I had a -- [what are the people?]
I don't know. Gibson? Or National? National used to make them in the old days for steel guitars, you know.
It had a high (unintelligible). It was kind of light brown.
It could have been a National.
Yeah, it could have been. I don't know because it's been so long.
Yeah. Tinker, what are you doing?
Did it have a pickup built in or did you have it mounted on it, like a De Armond mounted on it?
Like a De Armond. Tinker, cut it out.

She's okay. Do you remember when you first started playing electric? In some ways it's a change you know. You've got to play a little lighter, or you keep the volume down and you play hard, or a little lighter.
Because any time I'd go to a place and they didn't have an electric guitar for me to play, I'd get up close to that mike.
This way I'd come through more.
Sometimes I'd find myself hugging that mike.
Did you have any feedback problems when you --
No. What I'd do, I'd turn it down if it would get --
Uh-huh. I notice that right away you're using some longer notes.
Because one of the first things, of course, you get that sustained --
You know, instead of wherever -- you know, with an acoustic you might hit more notes. (SINGS)
You know, whereas with an electric (SINGS)
Yeah. I don't have to stretch.
Too long. When I want to cut it off, I'd
just cut my fingers down like that and cut it.
Wherever that note's coming from I'd try to snatch it off.
Yeah. The main reason, though -- you just felt it was a question of volume.
Yeah. I had to have volume if I was playing non-electric.
